design.purpose: Test whether a data-oriented compiler binding to numeric trait columns lowers update CPU while preserving the production commit-delay advantage.
design.relation: Follow-up to production V5; V5 source records and hashes remain unchanged.
design.order: Five fixed arm rotations and three-position size rotation per replication; see each page sequence.
design.dataLayout: The Snake model computes per-entity x/y into reusable Float64Array columns for every arm; no arm converts an object-per-entity position array into columns during measurement.

armsDescription.react: React 19.3.0 + React Compiler; per-segment useSyncExternalStore snapshots consuming the same x/y columns
armsDescription.runtime: runtime-discovered retained-VDOM bindings, one progress source, reading shared x/y columns
armsDescription.generated-vdom: existing OXC CSR compiled prop IDs through the generic ScalarSource/setSources path
armsDescription.columnar-vdom: OXC CSR prop IDs bound to contiguous Float64Array x/y columns; mount resolves entity rows to host writers; one setColumns batch per frame
armsDescription.direct: cached DOM hosts with direct left/top writes from the same columns

design.primaryMetric: update-to-commit milliseconds; React layout-effect timestamp, synchronous return for other arms
secondaryMetrics: per-page Chrome heap snapshots when available
design.analysis: Report five page summaries per cell; each page is the replication unit and its 300 RAFs are nested. Report paired per-replication ratios to React and all individual direction counts. No post-hoc outlier exclusions.
contracts: 300 samples with complete React commit coverage
output positions match the deterministic Snake model
host count and host identity remain stable during measured frames
visible Chrome page and stable environment across all trials
exclusions: layout, paint, GPU work, and physical presentation

collectionContext.serverInvocation: pnpm run build; pnpm run preview through Portless
